panels.rationale: Single lateral plain radiograph of the lumbosacral spine in a 4-day-old neonate from a case report titled 'Rachipagus Parasitic Twin With Epithelialized Myelomeningocele' (primary disease: myelomeningocele). The image is a real human-patient radiology image with an arrow indicating a posterior soft tissue mass at the site of vertebral (bony) dysraphism, i.e., open posterior spinal elements, which is the bony manifestation of myelomeningocele. The myelomeningocele is epithelialized (skin-covered/closed), a less-common closed form rather than the textbook open sac with neural placode, hence 'variant'. The mass also contains rudimentary osseous elements from the coexisting rachipagus parasitic twin, captured as a proposed finding; the dysraphic spinal defect itself still supports attribution to myelomeningocele. Radiograph, so skin tone is not assessable and is not inferred from the Ethiopian origin; ethnicity is not stated in the caption or in-text (only in the title), so stated_ethnicity is null. Confidence is moderately high given the parasitic-twin overlap, but the vertebral dysraphism is an explicit captioned manifestation of myelomeningocele. [raw subtype: epithelialized]

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient. Panel-specific caption and in-text explicitly describe a cicatrized/epithelialized midline lumbar mass (a healed myelomeningocele) with adjacent hypertrichosis, which is a cutaneous stigmata of spinal dysraphism. The manifestation is attributed to myelomeningocele per the caption (the prior triage also noted it is myelomeningocele, not split cord malformation itself). A cicatrized/healed myelomeningocele mass is a recognized less-common (variant) presentation versus the classic open neural-placode sac; the closest vocabulary key is used for the structural lesion while the cicatrized nature and the hypertrichosis are captured as proposed findings because no myelomeningocele-specific hypertrichosis key exists. No age or ethnicity is stated; skin is visible and reads as medium (olive) though lighting is somewhat dim.

in_text_mentions: On physical examination, she had a cicatrized/epithelialized midline mass in the upper lumber region with hypertrichosis lateral to it, Figure 1. Her upper extremity motor function was normal but, in the lower extremities, she had no ankle dorsiflexion on either side, normal patellar reflexes, and absent Achilles reflexes.
